boardStatus: YES — a separate ABPN Clinical Neurophysiology subspecialty certification examination exists. ABPN states that applicants must be certified in general neurology or neurology with special qualification in child neurology by the prior year, complete one year of ACGME-accredited CNP fellowship training after neurology residency, and meet the stated licensing/training requirements. The ABPN continuing-certification exam offers standard, EEG-emphasis, or EMG-emphasis options; these are not verified entry fellowship tracks or initial-exam outlines. The ABCN has a separate certification system. ABPN epilepsy certification is another separate subspecialty. Current requirements must be checked at ABPN; this independent course confers none of the eligibility conditions.
boardEligibilityNotice: No board eligibility is conferred. ABPN initial CNP certification requires board certification in general Neurology or Neurology with Special Qualification in Child Neurology, plus the required one-year ACGME-accredited CNP fellowship after residency, licensure and other current ABPN rules. MGB’s own entry requirements are a separate program admission matter. Verify with ABPN and program leadership; this independent course is not ACGME accredited, does not satisfy fellowship time, does not guarantee exam passing and is not official ABPN content.
